Notes:-
1. The Group has three primary Operating segments i.e. Water Infrastructure, Urban Infrastructure and Trading activities.

2. (a) JITF Urban Waste Management (Jalandhar) Limited and JITF Urban Waste Management (Ferozepur) Limited

Arbitration proceedings were initiated by JITF Urban Waste Management (Jalandhar) Limited and JITF Urban Waste Management (Ferozepur) Limited (collectively referred to as “JUWML”) against the Municipal Corporations of Jalandhar and Ferozepur, respectively, in relation to their respective projects. The Arbitral Awards dated 15th January 2022 were pronounced in favor of JUWML, awarding Rs.20,444.21 lakhs (including Bank Guarantees amounting to Rs.500 lakhs) for Jalandhar and Rs.9,229.35 lakhs (including Bank Guarantees amounting to Rs.340 lakhs) for Ferozepur, along with applicable interest.
JUWML has also challenged certain portions of the Awards under Section 34, and initiated enforcement and execution proceedings before the District Court, Chandigarh. Both proceedings are currently pending for adjudication before the Additional District Court, Chandigarh.

(b) JITF Urban Waste Management (Bathinda) Ltd.

Due to unrectified continuous defaults under the Concession Agreement dated 23rd November 2011 by the Municipal Corporation, Bathinda (MCB), JITF Urban Waste Management (Bathinda) Ltd. (JUWMBL) issued a Termination Notice on 5th December 2018 (effective 19th January 2019) and subsequently invoked arbitration on 19th March 2019 against MCB and the Department of Local Government, Punjab (DoLG) and filed claim and counterclaims by the parties against each other.
The Arbitral Award in this matter was pronounced on 21st May 2025, wherein the Tribunal held that the termination of the contract by JUWMBL is illegal and directed JUWMBL to continue performing the contract until the expiry of the concession period or early termination in a valid manner.

The Tribunal further awarded the claim for tipping fee of Rs. 183.57 lacs along with interest in favour of JUWMBL. MCB’s counterclaim for land lease payment of Rs. 8.11 lacs together with interest from the date of filing of the Counterclaim on 31.07.2019, has also been accepted by Arbitral Tribunal.

JUWMBL continues its plant operations, and its petition under Section 34 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, challenging the Award is pending for adjudication before the District Court, Chandigarh.

4. During the financial year 2025-26, JWIL Infra Limited (JWIL), indirect subsidiary of the Company offered 37,85,000 stock options convertible into equal number of equity shares of JWIL of face value Rs 10/- each under the “JWIL ESOP Scheme 2025”, as approved by the shareholder through special resolution passed at the EGM held on November 10,2025 to the eligible employees of JWIL.

Share based payment expense for the quarter and half year ended September 30, 2026 is Rs. Rs. 2,464.33 Lakhs and Rs. 4,928.67 lakhs respectively (year ended March 31, 2026 is Rs. 4,592.17 lakhs) has been recognized and disclosed as Exceptional Item. Consequently, upon exercise of all options by all employees to whom employee stock options shall be granted and allotment of shares by JWIL to all such employees, the shareholding of the JITF Urban Infrastructure Services Limited (JUISL), also a material subsidiary of the Company, in JWIL will be diluted from 54.61% to 50.01%. However, JWIL shall continue to remain indirect subsidiary of the Company.
